text:
Every conversation about the Lightning right now starts with Nikita Kucherov and where he plays next. He is a pending free agent, his reported trade request has been public for weeks, and the past few days brought a wave of Montreal talk after Elliotte Friedman described a possible Kent Hughes plan to bring him to the Canadiens. Meanwhile the team in front of him is sliding: Tampa is winless in three, outscored 15-5, and was routed 6-2 by Ottawa at home last night. Our numbers call the slump partly real, with 47% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) in those games. Conor Geekie is out four to five months after shoulder surgery, and Pontus Holmberg and Erik Cernak are out too.

Florida's week has been loud for other reasons. Matthew Tkachuk escaped discipline for his hit on Ottawa's Tyler Kleven, and Sportsnet was among those asking whether he should have been fined. On the ice the Panthers have won three straight, the last two with Aleksander Barkov and Brad Marchand back from injury, and Sam Bennett has five goals in his last three games, including the winner in Washington last night that survived a hand-pass review and gave him 200 for his career. Our numbers only half believe the run: 52% of the expected goals across the three wins. Tkachuk plays his 700th game tonight, Seth Jones is one point from 500, and Garnet Hathaway is out after a leg-on-leg collision, per Paul Maurice via NHL.com's Tom Gulitti.

Both teams played last night, so neither gets the rest edge, and our numbers have both tired. Andrei Vasilevskiy is 2.5 goals above expected after saving 23 above expected last season; Akira Schmid sits right at zero.

The thing to watch is the penalty box. Florida takes 5.1 penalties a game and draws 5.0, and its power play makes 1.04 expected goals a game. Tampa's penalty kill allows 0.57. Jake Guentzel brings a five-game point streak across the state, and Brandon Hagel is back from injured reserve.
headline: Kucherov noise, Tkachuk noise, and a tired Florida derby
